name: Contoro Robotics
status: current public product/company source located; legal and operating status not independently verified
product: A managed trailer/container-unloading service combining an integrated robotic cell, AI and company remote intervention, priced per container without upfront capital.
mission: The company states that it seeks to address the customer problem represented by its current product: AI-guided robots unload trailers and containers; deployments combine autonomy and remote assistance.
customerProblem: Engineer perception, control and task-specific hardware around the operational workflow in logistics & warehousing.
workflow: Unloading non-palletized boxes from truck trailers and shipping containers, with remote human help for exceptions.
initialTargetCustomer: warehouse, parcel, port or logistics operators
businessModel: Per-container unloading service with no upfront capital, as stated by the company; price not public.
goToMarket: direct/partner route unresolved from reviewed public sources
namedCustomers: KUKA's detailed case study identifies States Logistics as operating Contoro's unloading solution and quotes the customer on production benefits; the system combines a KUKA arm with Contoro software, sensors, custom gripper and mobile base
fundingBasis: Last disclosed round — later strategic investment undisclosed
fundingNote: One source-checked USD financing event; not total funding or a complete round history.
fundingRaw: $12M Series A announced 25 March 2025; a later strategic investment was announced without an amount
thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: A managed trailer/container-unloading service combining an integrated robotic cell, AI and company remote intervention, priced per container without upfront capital. The company positions it against this problem: Engineer perception, control and task-specific hardware around the operational workflow in logistics & warehousing. Verified current scope: end-to-end unloading workflow. Stated ambition: unresolved beyond current company positioning. Public evidence supports responsibility for hardware, end effectors/tooling, models/policies, integration, remote operations and hardware financing/RaaS; supports only partial/shared responsibility for commissioning/qualification; does not establish responsibility for robot body, simulation/training and ongoing support/maintenance. Overall integration responsibility is classified as shared. Commercial evidence: 3_partner_confirmed_or_customer_pilot; technical evidence: 4_named_partner_confirmed. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Partial integration comparator: public evidence supports a company role in integration or qualification, but responsibility is shared with a customer, OEM or partner. Commercial evidence is 3_partner_confirmed_or_customer_pilot; whole-workflow prime responsibility is not established.
evidenceGaps: No independent customer evidence found in reviewed sources; integration, commissioning, support, pricing and repeatability remain unverified where not stated. | Verifier A unresolved claim types: performance_metric
